chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said: I asked al-Rida 'Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them): "O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about the Qur'an. Is it uncreated or created?"
He (AS) replied: "It is neither uncreated nor created; rather it is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.مَخْلُوقٌ: Created (brought into existence by a creator)

ai.seo_question: Is the Quran created or uncreated according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) resolves the Mu'tazili-Kharijite debate by defining the Qur'an as the eternal 'Speech of God' (Kalam Allah), distinct from created entities yet not identical to His essence, thereby preserving divine unity. This position aligns with the mainstream Shia theological view that the Qur'an is an attribute of God's action, eternal in its reality but manifested in time through revelation. The statement underscores the Qur'an's status as the direct, uncreated discourse of Allah, avoiding the pitfalls of both tashbih (anthropomorphism) and ta'til (denial of attributes).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Ahmad Ziyad ibn Ja`far al-Hamdani (ra) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim said, on the authority of his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of `Ali ibn Ma`bad, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Khalid that I asked al-Rida `Ali ibn Musa (AS): “O son of the Messenger of Allah! Tell me about the Qur’an. Is it a creator or created?”
Therefore, he (AS) replied, “It is neither a creator nor created; rather it is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”
